nodes.title: Ordinary global multiplicity one for GL(n)
nodes.statement: For an irreducible admissible smooth representation π of GL_n(𝔸_K), K a number field, its multiplicity in the smooth cuspidal spectrum with fixed central character is at most one. If π is cuspidal, the multiplicity is one: any two nonzero equivariant embeddings into that cusp space differ by a nonzero scalar and have the same image. This is the ordinary multiplicity theorem; it assumes the same global representation, rather than cofinite local agreement.
hypotheses: n≥1; K a number field; characteristic-zero complex automorphic forms. Work with the unitary central-character Hilbert realization or an explicitly fixed norm twist.

Use continuous equivariant embeddings and continuous Whittaker functionals on the smooth moderate-growth globalizations at infinity. Multiplicity in the Hilbert spectrum is compared through the existing AS.4/AF.3 realization, not a freely chosen numerical function.
proofSteps: For two cuspidal embeddings i₁,i₂, compose with evaluation at the identity of their Whittaker coefficients. Fourier reconstruction implies both functionals are nonzero.
Flath factorization and continuous local Whittaker uniqueness make the two global functionals proportional by a scalar c≠0.

Apply the same equality to every translate π(g)v, then reconstruct the cusp forms by their Fourier expansions: i₁(v)=c·i₂(v) for every v. Thus the two images agree and the embedding space has dimension at most one; a cuspidal occurrence gives equality. For n=1, evaluation at the identity directly determines a function with its fixed character.
acceptance: Rescaling an embedding by c≠0 gives the same cuspidal subrepresentation.
A two-dimensional space of level invariants does not change the global multiplicity from one.
Without a cuspidal occurrence the multiplicity may be zero; no occurrence is asserted for every admissible representation.

gaps.title: G1: actual arithmetic/representation interfaces
gaps.detail: The named SR, AA, AF and GlobalNumberFields interfaces are planned suppliers, not accepted implementations. Their exact native carriers, coefficient hypotheses, completed tensor topology and measure transport must be supplied before full signatures can be elaborated. The suggested file uses native archimedean spaces and generic integral/representation formula specializations, and explicitly names the remaining unstatable declarations.

gaps.title: G2: local-field inverse duality proof
gaps.detail: Tate states local self-duality using general LCA theory. The plan specifies a finite-lattice quotient inverse construction; its continuity/surjectivity proof has not been decomposed from a complete read primary proof. The native PontryaginDual carrier supplies no self-duality theorem. Fractional-ideal inverse-different identities require the GNF/LocalFields arithmetic comparison. The trace-dual conductor input belongs to LocalFieldsRamification Layer3; completed trace compatibility is explicitly requested. The AL.0 local self-duality statement is restricted to number-field completions. The adelic topological self-duality transport from the local inverse maps, including restricted-product character continuity and discreteness of the annihilator of the compact quotient, remains a precise refinement of the Poisson proof. Its finite-cardinality conclusion is not inferred from finite vector-space dimension.

gaps.title: G3: point-supported distributions
gaps.detail: The structure theorem behind Kudla Lemma3.3 is cited to Friedlander but its original proof source is unread. The finite-order jet argument is a proof outline, not closure. Invariant continuous-distribution uniqueness on the archimedean punctured line is not the native Haar-measure predicate: prove it, for example by convolution with compactly supported smooth approximate identities and continuity. review.reason: As E15 says, the two cases do not exhaust unitary pairs, but the missing value is determined. If π1 ≅ π2⊗λ with λ unramified, unitarity of both forces λ = α^{deg∘det} with |α| = 1, and L(π1×π2^∨, z) = L(π2×π2^∨, α'z) with |α'| = 1, so every zero and pole radius is as for π1 = π2. The proof reduces the argument to π1 = π2 without loss of generality and finishes using the equivalence Π1∼Π2 ⇔ (ν1=ν2 and π1∼π2). These steps already prove the missing case, so the printed '=' is a slip for '∼'. The only use, Theorem 6.4.1, is for good representatives, where Π_i ≠ Π_j implies Π_i ≁ Π_j. Radius counts were recomputed for (n, ν1, ν2, g, f) = (2,3,1,2,2), (2,2,2,2,1), (3,1,1,3,3) and (1,4,4,2,1). The recorded kind 'gap' and affects 'a stated result' overstate it.

sourceCorrections.reason: q^s + q^{−s} = 2cosh(s log q) = 2Σ_{j≥0}(s log q)^{2j}/(2j)!, so subtracting the constant 2 gives 2Σ_{j≥1}(s log q)^{2j}/(2j)!, not /j!. sourceCorrections.printed: TheoremB.2 assumes π is a nontrivial self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸). Its proof infers that the standard L(π,s) is entire from cuspidality and nontriviality.
sourceCorrections.correction: Add the hypothesis that L(π, s) is entire. It is automatic for n ≥ 2; for n = 1 over a function field it excludes the unitary characters factoring through the degree, such as (−1)^{deg}.
sourceCorrections.reason: π = (−1)^{deg} on GL_1 over a function field (the quadratic character of the constant-field extension) is nontrivial, cuspidal and self-dual, but L(π, s) = Z_X(−q^{−s}) has poles. For X = P¹, Λ(π, 1/2 + t) = 1/(q^t + q^{−t} + q^{1/2} + q^{−1/2}), so Λ″(π, 1/2) = −2(log q)²/(2 + q^{1/2} + q^{−1/2})² < 0 (−0.1300 for q = 3), contradicting (1). Theorem 1.7 uses only GL_2 cuspidal L-functions and is unaffected. Also in arXiv v3.

checked.note: The additive subgroup carrier permits a trivial character and a degenerate pairing; the real integer lattice disproves an R-submodule carrier.
Membership is exactly triviality on every element of U, with no topological hypothesis.
Closedness follows from continuous equality loci and arbitrary intersections, not finite generation of U.
Joint local constancy and compactness allow the tube lemma; an infinite intersection of open fibers would be invalid.
The native negative-kernel translation identity forces vanishing when the period phase is nontrivial.
Ordinary Fourier support lies in the annihilator; topological support is its closure and needs closedness.
The Haar orthogonality formula remains valid for the native totalized integral; the coefficient is μ.real(U).
For f(v−a), the native transform has phase ψ(−L(a,w)); the sign agrees with the pinned definition.
Multiplication by ψ(L(v,b)) shifts the native transform from w to w−b.
Support in a subgroup gives periods in its annihilator without presupposing biduality.
Compact support is bounded in a lattice and hence has an open annihilator; this gives local constancy.
A common open period lattice gives compact annihilator support; a compact-open carrier is required.
The lattice volume product gives reflection after two transforms; it does not follow from support alone.
Finite-place functions reuse the SR.1 carrier; real/complex functions reuse SchwartzMap with the chosen pairing.
